2026 one in christ, united in mission this weekend, we celebrate mission sunday, a special day when catholics throughout the world come together in prayer & solidarity to support the church’s missionary work. this year marks the 100th anniversary of world mission sunday, established by pope pius xi in 1926. to mark this centenary, pope leo xiv has chosen the theme “one in christ, united in mission.” in his message for this special anniversary, pope leo reminds us that the mission of the church belongs to all of us. through baptism, every christian is called to share god's love & bring the message of the gospel to others. world mission sunday is an opportunity to remember the many missionaries who dedicate their lives to serving communities throughout the world, often in places facing great poverty & hardship. through our prayers, generosity & practical support, we can all play a part in their work. mission begins in our own everyday lives, through simple acts of kindness, compassion & care for others. together, we are one in christ & united in mission. athenry simanjiro partnership athenry–simanjiro partnership, first established in november 2005, is now in its 21st year. we are a registered charity. over the years, with the incredible generosity of the people of athenry & beyond, we've been able to support the community in simanjiro, north-east tanzania, in so many meaningful ways. celebrating our partnership: last year, fr. lawrence from simanjiro visited the parish. a wonderful display detailing the partnership's work is available to view in the church, a testament to athenry's generosity. making a real difference: the partnership directly connects with the local community to fund education & healthcare, with projects also including supplying fresh water & building the church. electricity only arrived there in 2021. a few things that make our partnership unique are: 100% direct donation: every single euro donated goes directly to simanjiro. self-funded travel: all who travel there pay their ownway – it's a core principle of the organisation. local partnership: we work proudly alongside our on-the- ground partners, the divine word missionaries, led by fr. bienvenue and fr. rex. support our future: thank you all once again for your kindness, generosity and commitment over the past 20 years. we look forward to continuing this wonderful partnership into the future. your support makes a real difference. if you would like to find out more, please see the board at the back of athenry church (which includes a donation box), contact us on

, or visit our facebook page. october – month of the holy rosary our lady of the rosary, pray for us. as we continue through the month of the holy rosary, we are reminded to keep this beautiful prayer in mind & make a little space for it in our daily lives. whether praying a full rosary or one decade, we can take a few quiet moments to reflect & bring our joys, worries & intentions to god. let’s make a special effort to find time for the rosary, at home, with our families or whenever a quiet moment presents itself. first holy communion 2027: grow in love a reminder to parents of children preparing for their first holy communion next may that our registration meeting for parents takes place on tuesday 20th october. details have been communicated to families through the schools. we look forward to meeting all the parents and beginning this special journey of preparation with the children and their families. our monthly grow in love masses will begin next weekend. candlelight holy hour annual novena for deceased — athenry church the annual novena for the deceased takes place from all souls’ day mon. 2nd — wed. 11th november at 10:00am masses. during this special time of prayer, we remember our deceased family members, friends & parishioners. lists to write names of your deceased loved ones are now available in both churches. these can be returned before or during the novena. during mass times there will be a box available at the front of the altar. daily intentions return thursday 12th. items for our church newsletter priority is always given to church and diocesan notices. local

sliocht as leabhar ísáia fáidh -- 25:6-10 réiteoidh tiarna na slua féasta mór ar an sliabh seo le haghaidh na gciníocha go léir, beidh scoth na beatha ann agus togha an fhíona, beatha shaibhir agus bhlasta, fíon nach bhfuil a bhualadh le fáil.
tógfaidh sé leis den sliabh seo an lionndubh atá mar bheadh clóca ar an domhan go léir agus an taiséadach atá timpeall na náisiún go léir, cuirfidh sé an bás ar ceal.
briathar an tiarna. freagra: buíochas le dia salm le freagra: i dteach an tiarna a mhairfidh mé, go brách na breithe. ‘sé’n tiarna m’aoire, ní bheidh aon uireasa orm.
glanfaidh dia na deora de chuile éadan, ní fhágfaidh sé a phobal faoi náire in aon áit ar fud an domhain, mar sé an tiar na a dúirt.
fiú dá siúlfainn i ngleann an dorchadais níor bhaol dom an t-olc agus tú ansin le do shlat is do bhachall, le sólás a thabhairt dom.
déarfar an lásin, breathnaígí, sé árn diaé, a raibh muid ag súil le slánú uaidh; sé an tiarna é ar chuir muid ár muinín as.
agus ní fhágfaidh mo dhia easpa oraibhse as a fhlúirse féin trí íosa críost. moladh go deo le dia, árn a thair.
fr réitigh tú féasta dom, i bhfianaise mo naimhde, chuir túola ar mo cheann; tá mo chupán ag cur thar maoil.
